question: Lagos has more residents than the whole of Ghana.

evidence.title: 2021 Population and Housing Census: General Report
evidence.excerpt: The 2021 Population and Housing Census enumerated 30,832,019 persons in Ghana, an increase of 6.2 million over the 2010 census figure.

evidence.title: About Lagos State
evidence.excerpt: Lagos State is home to an estimated 20 million people, making it one of the largest urban areas in Africa, though estimates vary widely.

evidence.title: World Urbanization Prospects: Lagos
evidence.excerpt: The Lagos urban agglomeration was estimated at 13.9 million residents in 2018, projected to grow rapidly through 2030.

evidence.title: How fast is Lagos really growing?
evidence.excerpt: Counting Lagos is notoriously hard; figures from 12 million to 21 million are quoted depending on boundaries and sources.

turns.text: Lagos State's own figure is about 20 million people (ev2), and growth there has been explosive. Some estimates of the metro area run past 21 million (ev4), which would rival a mid-sized country.
Ghana's 2021 census counted 30.8 million people (ev1). Even the highest Lagos estimate, about 21 million (ev4), falls roughly 10 million short. The UN put the city at 13.9 million (ev3).
Counting Lagos is uncertain (ev4), so the claim could hold under the broadest boundary. But I concede no source puts Lagos above 30 million.
Uncertainty about Lagos spans 12 to 21 million. None of it approaches Ghana's census total of 30.8 million. The claim is false by a wide margin.
Ghana's census counts 30.8 million people. The highest credible Lagos estimate is about 21 million. Even with uncertain city boundaries, Lagos is far smaller than Ghana.

rationale: Ghana's 2021 census counted 30.8 million people. Even the biggest estimates for Lagos are about 21 million, so the claim is false.
